Credit card cell phone insurance compared

By
Nick Reyes and Tim Steinke
-
September 2, 2026
123
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:12
Instaread

These days, your cell phone may be among your most expensive possessions. Coverage for damage or theft can be worthwhile for those who are prone to damaging their phone and/or who want peace of mind about replacement costs. Luckily, many rewards credit cards offer strong cell phone insurance coverage as part of their standard benefits.

Nick wrote about an experience using credit card cell phone insurance protection a couple of years ago. While his claim was ultimately approved, he concluded that it wasn’t really a win because he felt he had made a poor choice in which card he used, which had a large deductible compared to the repair cost of his phone. He’d have been better off self-insuring and earning more points per dollar on his bill.

This post includes an easy-to-use chart and is a quick-reference resource on what you need to know about credit card cell phone insurance, and hopefully avoid making the same mistake.

Best Credit Card Purchase Protections

Credit card cell phone insurance basics

As you can see in the chart below, many credit cards (and, in some cases, debit and secured cards) offer cell phone insurance, but that insurance is not created equal. Per-claim caps and deductibles vary widely.

Most cards require you to pay your monthly bill in full with the credit card providing coverage. When coverage begins varies; with some cards it begins the day after you pay your cell phone bill and continues through the end of the following calendar month. Most cards offer coverage that begins on the first day of the next calendar month after you pay your bill.

Confirm how coverage works with your chosen card before you need to file a claim.

Additional notes on credit card cell phone insurance

If your card offers cell phone insurance, you should find the details on cell phone coverage somewhere in your guide to benefits. That said, how many of us keep the guide to benefits handy? Some issuers make that guide to benefits available online, but not all do. That makes a post like this challenging, as you could have cards in your wallet that offer it without an easy way to know. The chart above shows cards known to carry coverage, but additional cards almost certainly have it as well.

If you still have the Guide to Benefits that came with your credit card, hopefully you can find cell phone protection details there. And in the case of many of the cards in the chart above, you can easily confirm coverage information on the issuer’s website.

Will cell phone coverage apply if you only pay part of your bill with your qualifying credit card?

Officially, cell phone insurance benefits almost always require you to pay your cell phone bill in full with the card offering coverage. A common question is whether coverage applies if you use more than one card to pay the bill. For instance, the American Express Business Platinum card offers a monthly $10 credit for wireless services. If you have more than one Business Platinum card, will paying with multiple cards disqualify you from coverage?

In our experience, coverage has been extended when paying the full amount shown on the monthly bill when it is generated, but you can pay with more than one card and still accomplish that:

  • Pay your bill in full with a card that offers cell phone coverage.
  • After the bill has a $0 balance, make additional payments. For example, you could use a Business Platinum card to make an additional $10 payment, bringing the balance down to -$10.
  • When the next monthly bill generates, that -$10 balance carries forward, and the total shown on the new monthly bill is $10 less because of the negative balance carry-forward.
  • Pay the full amount on a credit card offering cell phone protection.
  • Rinse, wash, repeat.

We can’t guarantee that this won’t disqualify you from coverage, but we’ve both had to make a claim after paying this way, showing the total due at the top and the balance forward carry-over beneath that. In both cases, our claim was approved. Ultimately, whether your claim qualifies for coverage is up to a claims adjuster/benefits administrator.

Bottom line

Credit card cell phone insurance is part of the benefits offered on many credit cards. In many cases, the most valuable item people carry day to day is their phone, and coverage for damage or theft can really ease the sting if your phone is completely destroyed.

On the other hand, consider the deductible and coverage limits relative to the cost of repairing or replacing your phone, the category bonus you may be able to trigger on a credit card that doesn’t offer cell phone insurance, and any debit autopay discounts you may lose. Some will prefer to self-insure and use a card that earns an excellent category bonus rather than worry about insurance.

It’s worth running the numbers to see how much you sacrifice in potential rewards by using a card that earns fewer points to pay your bill or by losing your autopay discount, especially if you have several expensive phones on your plan.
